angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,534,431 km at 54.73 pc = 1.84 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94005: distance 54.734 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.019), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 54.734 +/- 1.04 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 17.6582 +/- 0.2460 mas (same row, RUWE 1.59), 71.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.83 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94005: radius 10.83 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 50.332 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,534,431 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4675 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94005: effective temperature 4675 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.051) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94005: effective temperature 4675 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.051) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.64 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 3 published values span log g 2.59 to 2.643, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
